correctness.rationale: For all R>=r>0 and R-r<s<R+r in R^3, a<b makes each ball-containment squared-distance function strictly concave; the polar branch obeys its exact endpoint/latitude maxima and the two-latitude branch has a unique monotone scalar root and both exact equalities. The contact measures at u,v satisfying uv=-1/3 are positive, centered and isotropic; supporting-plane integration and trace/AM-GM proves the candidate is globally unique among unrestricted ellipsoids. Endpoint equal-radius specialization and 1170 parameter diagnostics verified by checker; sampled calculations are not universal proof. Tests exclude nested and tangent balls.

Limit of exhaustive historical coverage explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: Undiscovered equivalent older extremal-ellipse construction may exist under a sphere-intersection or lens approximation name; searches cannot establish global priority.
The full historical Kahan 1968 article was not accessed. Its accessible scope is centered and enclosing rather than the present uncentered and inscribed problem.
Extensions to arbitrary dimension, more than two balls and measurement noise are neither proved nor claimed.

value.rationale: The geometric problem is the exact unrestricted maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoid of the natural intersection of two unequal Euclidean balls, closing the important unequal-radius case missing from exact symmetric-lens work. The R/r=3 threshold separates fundamentally different polar-contact and two-circle regimes, with exact formulas and contact certificates useful in geometric approximation and optimization; not merely a special numerical computation.
